why: NOT a book error — a defect in OUR OWN linear transcription of the book's printed dot structure, caught by re-counting electrons against the worked example's own Step I. The book prints each terminal oxygen of the all-single-bonded form with THREE lone pairs (dots above, dots below, and a colon on the outside); the first rendering carried only two on each, which totals 14 valence electrons and so contradicts the '5 + (2x6) + 1 = 18 electrons' this very solution derives one line above. The outer lone pairs are restored, giving 6 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 6 = 18 electrons, with nitrogen still short of an octet — which is exactly the state Step III goes on to describe. Nothing about the book's own working changes, so no errata bracket is owed.

NOT a book error — a defect in OUR OWN transcription. The book's Step II prints the skeletal structure of CO as `:C:O:` with a COLON (a shared electron pair) between the C and the O, alongside the equivalent dash form `:C-O:`. The first rendering used a single centred dot, which denotes one electron rather than the shared pair, and so disagrees with the dash form printed immediately beside it. Corrected to the colon the page actually carries.
